title: Remote hire quickstart pocket — 14d checklist
content:
Purpose:
Quick, scannable 14-day onboarding + interview handoff bundle for remote hires (ICs and entry-level managers). Designed for hiring managers + onboarding buddies to run with minimal back-and-forth. Not exhaustive — a pocket guide.

High-level goals (first 14 days):
- Get candidate productive on one measurable task (ticket/OKR slice).
- Confirm access + tooling (IDE, repo, VPN, calendar, email).
- Build 1–2 human touchpoints (manager 1:1, buddy pairing, team intro).
- Validate culture fit and role clarity via lightweight check-ins (manager + hiring partner).

Owner notes / quick context:
- Use for remote hires joining outside main office hours (different timezones).
- Prioritize async artifacts (recorded team intro, checklist links) so new hire can self-serve.
- Hiring partner: loop in if any access or payroll hiccups by day 2.

Day-by-day checklist (condensed):
Day -1 (Offer accepted):
  - Send Welcome packet + 48hr expectations doc (link template).
  - Confirm start date, timezone, rough first-week schedule.
  - HR to submit equipment request; manager to confirm workspace stipend.

Day 0 (First day):
  - IT: laptop shipped or confirm pickup + simple install checklist link.
  - People Ops: payroll & benefits onboarding email sent (with deadlines).
  - Manager: 30-min welcome intro (team context, immediate first task, who to ping).
  - Buddy: intro message + shared 1-pager (team norms, async windows, key docs).
  - Mandatory trainings queued (security, code of conduct).

Day 1–3:
  - Access verification: repo read, issue tracker, VPN, calendar, badge (if applicable).
  - Small first task assigned (bug triage, doc edit, infra smoke test) — measurable, <8 hours.
  - Schedule recurring 1:1s: manager weekly, buddy daily check-ins for first 2 weeks.
  - Team intro async: post in #team with quick bio + priorities.

Day 4–7:
  - Technical onboarding: walkthrough of main repo, local dev guide, runbook link.
  - Interviewer follow-up: hiring manager + hiring partner do a 30-min calibration using the rubric below — confirm red flags or follow-ups.
  - Checkpoint: did hire complete first task? If not, identify blockers and resolve within 48 hours.

Day 8–14:
  - Impact sprint: assign small cross-team task (deliverable + acceptance criteria).
  - Skills recap: manager documents early signals (skills, ramp blockers, culture fit) and shares with recruiting/hiring partner.
  - First retro (end of week 2): 30-min alignment with manager, buddy, people ops — capture wins and friction.

Interview handoff rubric (one-pager for hiring manager to close loop):
Scoring: 1–4 (1 = mismatch, 4 = strong match). Use these three lenses and an overall disposition.
- Role competence (technical skills / core responsibilities): examples: can deliver an isolated task, reads code, writes clear PRs.
- Learning & autonomy: picks up new code quickly, asks clarifying Qs, can work async.
- Team fit & communication: clarity in async comms, responsiveness, empathy.

Red-flag triggers (fast action):
- Unable to get basic access after 3 business days -> escalate to IT & hiring partner.
- Repeated missed check-ins without notice -> manager documents and sets 1:1 expectations.
- Behavioral concerns (team mismatch, unwillingness to accept feedback) -> hiring partner consult within 72 hours.

Quick scorecard template (to paste into candidate file):
- Competence: X/4
- Learning/autonomy: X/4
- Communication/fit: X/4
- Overall hire disposition: Hire / Monitor / Offboard
- 1–2 concrete next steps for week 3 (ramp plan)

Manager and buddy playbook (short):
Manager:
- Day 0: set expectations for 14-day milestone and first deliverable.
- Weekly: send written summary of priorities and feedback.
- Document early ramp notes in candidate file (first 14d signals).

Buddy:
- Daily quick async check-in (first week) + one 30-min pairing session.
- Maintain a short "common gotchas" doc in the repo specific to the team.

Common templates (copyable):
- Slack welcome (channel message): "Welcome @NAME 🎉 — joining as [role]. They'll be working on [project]. Please give a warm welcome and add any intro notes. Key docs: [link]."
- Manager first message: short agenda + 1 immediate task + 3 people to meet week 1.
- Escalation note to HR: brief problem summary + what we've tried + desired outcome.

Equipment & admin checklist (quick):
- Laptop + charger received and imaged
- VPN & MFA enabled
- Company email & calendar working
- Dev keys / repo access
- Slack/Zoom profiles set
- Payroll & benefits forms completed

Success signals to capture by day 14 (for hiring partner):
- Completed first task with reviewer feedback published
- Manager assessment: green/amber/red plus written note
- Buddy note: 1–2 onboarding friction points
- New hire self-assessment: 3 things going well, 1 ask for help

Edge cases & notes to self (todo items):
- For hires in restrictive countries, confirm tax/payment path before day 0 (common blocker).
- Consider staggered onboarding for cross-timezone teammates (recorded intros + flexible pair windows).
- If role is remote manager, add an extra leadership calibration check by week 2 with hiring partner.

Unresolved decisions / questions in this draft:
- Do we require manager to complete a formal "first-14d sign-off" form for all ICs? (pros/cons listed inline)
- Should we centralize the small first task templates in one repo or leave team-owned?

Quick links (for copy/paste):
- Offer + welcome templates: confluence:HR-offer-templates
- IT checklist script: github:infrastructure/onboard-scripts#laptop-image
- First task examples bank: drive:shared/first-task-library

If this doc is useful, next steps:
1) People Ops to produce a printable 1-pager (A4) with day 0–3 essentials.
2) Engineering onboarding owners to add 2 standardized first tasks per sub-team.
3) Add a short manager sign-off checkbox to the candidate file for auditability.

Notes: written as a compact, manager-facing pocket guide. Keep it lightweight; we want high compliance for remote hires.

[end of doc]
